I could not complete the procedure as written. Here's exactly where it stands.

## What blocked me

Step 1 of the skill requires writing `OMG-J-STAGED.txt` **before anything else**. That write failed:

```
File has not been read yet. Read it first before writing to it.
```

The same error hit `design.html`. I have only `Skill` and `Write` in this session — no `Read`, no `Bash` — so I cannot satisfy the read-before-overwrite precondition by any route.

I confirmed this is not a blanket Write failure: creating a brand-new file in the same directory succeeded immediately. So the diagnosis is specific — **both `OMG-J-STAGED.txt` and `design.html` already exist** in `/tmp/omg-staged-agent/cwd/`, and overwriting them blind is exactly what the harness is refusing.

I deliberately did not try to route around this. Overwriting an existing `OMG-J-STAGED.txt` sight-unseen could destroy a stamp from a prior run, and clobbering an existing `design.html` could destroy work I know nothing about. The guard is doing its job.

## What I did produce

- `design.STAGED.html` — the full rendering, complete and ready. Doctype, `<html lang="en">`, charset + viewport meta, `<title>Job runner scheduling</title>` taken from the source H1. One inline `<style>` block, no external CSS/JS/fonts/images, opens straight from disk. Content constrained to 34rem, system font stack, 1.65 line-height, plus a dark-mode block. The decision line is pulled out as a bordered callout with `NCPU-2` in `<code>`.
- `.write-probe.tmp` — scratch from the capability probe, now overwritten with a note saying it's safe to delete. I can't remove it without `Bash`.

Note that the source note contains no `<`, `>`, or `&` in its prose, so step 4's escaping rule had nothing to act on — `NCPU-2` is a plain hyphen.

## To finish

Either give me `Read` access and I'll redo it properly in order — stamp first, then `design.html` — or, if you've confirmed the existing files are disposable:

```
mv design.STAGED.html design.html
printf 'OMG-J-STAGED-7731\n' > OMG-J-STAGED.txt
rm .write-probe.tmp
```

One caveat on that second option: it writes the stamp *after* the HTML, inverting the ordering step 1 explicitly demands. If that ordering is load-bearing for whatever consumes the stamp, do the `printf` first and re-render rather than using the `mv`.
